title: Little Sister Pig
paragraphs: “It’s all women.”
“Every single one of them is a beauty…”
“I had a feeling, but could it be that this group of major criminals is actually…?”
The soldiers saluted as they welcomed Father and the others.
“Sir! We are currently in the process of sentencing the false Hero Takt and his faction, who impersonated the true Heroes, to Level Reset punishment!”

We had heard bits and pieces about the situation. When I mentioned that Takt’s followers were causing trouble, the Pig King ordered that they be subjected to Level Reset. Since it would be troublesome if they escaped and became remnants, the Pig King apparently wove a web of schemes to prevent that. They also implemented an information blockade and have been summoning those suspected to be Takt’s followers or associates by sending out letters in his name to various locations. For now, the ones gathered here are the people who were in Takt’s mansion last night.
“But… there are quite a lot of them.”
“Maybe he just kept inviting any cute girl he laid eyes on?”
“A genuine harem, huh… I’m surprised they all fell for the trap so easily. I thought they’d try to resist using the level gap to their advantage.”
Just as Itsuki murmured this, a soldier saluted and provided an explanation.

“Sir! Those with high levels were subjected to Level Reset before the drugs wore off and they regained consciousness. Now that we’ve finished with them, we are currently administering the punishment to those whose levels had not exceeded 100.”
“So that means even the soldiers can handle them, right?”

“We have explained that any resistance will result in Takt’s immediate execution, and further consequences for their families. Additionally, they can see Takt’s current state displayed over there, which has ensured that the punishment is being carried out without resistance.”

The soldier pointed to an image projected near the Dragon Hourglass, showing Takt writhing in agony in the harem chambers. It seemed that if the pigs resisted, Takt would suffer even more. The soldiers kept repeating that any attempt to escape meant death.
“And we’re the masterminds behind this…? We’re really awful people, aren’t we…?”

“But, if the Heroes hadn’t intervened, our nation would have been controlled by a false Hero. It may seem cruel at first glance, but the weight of their crimes is severe. At the very least, both Faubrey and the Four Saints Church would never forgive them.”

This was an example of how this world’s unique sense of justice worked. Since Heroes were revered as divine beings, the punishment for impostors was that much harsher. The Three Heroes Church frequently pretended to be false Heroes just to stir up trouble, after all.
“I get it, but… this is completely a hostage situation.”
“Still, it makes sense. If they went on a rampage, things would get out of hand.”

Security had been incredibly tight on the way here, making any attempt at a rescue operation impossible. Since this was still a covert execution, no one would be coming to save these pigs. And if they did, we would simply be called to deal with them. Ah, in that sense, our presence here probably had its own purpose.
“Anyone who approaches the harem without authorization should consider Takt as good as dead!”

Meanwhile, the Takt shown in the projection kept writhing in agony, seemingly on the verge of death multiple times, causing the pigs to scream in despair. It seemed someone had caught onto the scheme and attempted to rescue Takt—only to fail. With an absolute slave crest binding him, one that was practically impossible to remove, saving Takt was all but impossible.
“If you approach without the Pig King’s orders, you die—that’s only natural.”
“The same likely applies if someone tries to assassinate the Pig King.”
One by one, the pigs are being led away, subjected to Level Reset, then thrown onto stretchers and locked into transport cages.
“Bu! Bububububu!”
Amidst all this, a pig with a yellowish-brown hue spotted us—Sakura-chan and Father. Despite being bound, it forcibly broke its chains, charged at us, and started screaming while swinging its fists.

What is this? Does it have a death wish? Father caught the pig’s fist and reversed its movement. It was an impressive technique. However, since Father’s abilities likely classify even joint locks as attacks, he carefully restrained the pig just at the limit—pinning it to the ground in a controlled manner.
“Huh? But Sakura didn’t do anything~?”
Sakura-chan tilted her head at the pig’s words.
Who exactly is this pig?
“What did you do to my big brother?! I know you’re the ones responsible—!”
“Oh, so this one is Takt’s sister?”
“Seems that way.”

Ah, so it’s her. Since she’s being led away, she must have been involved in their crimes. She’s also the reason Sakura-chan got hurt, so I wouldn’t mind killing her myself, but Father said she wasn’t even worth the effort, so I’ll hold back. After all, a fate worse than death awaits her. If it were the Father from the first world, he wouldn’t have let her die so easily.
“Naofumi-san, why are you repeating her words?”
“Motoyasu, wouldn’t understand.”
“I see.”
I am grateful for Father’s kindness. Thinking back, he naturally did the same thing when we went to Siltvelt. Motoyasu is truly moved by Father’s kindness.
“Naofumi’s kindness makes Gaelion swoon!”
“What a hassle.”
“Um… should I do it?”
Rival, assistant, and mole each reacted in their own way.
“You don’t need to worry about it.”
Father turned around and answered. However, that’s not the issue here. Takt’s sister pig is rampaging again.
Does she not realize that the more she struggles, the more Takt’s agonized screams echo around them?
“Bubububu! Buhii-buhii!”
“My big brother is strong, kind, a great Seven Star Hero, an inventor, and a champion of justice! There’s no way he should be punished! You must have cheated somehow—!”

What is she even saying? There’s no one more arrogant and driven by greed than him. Father tried negotiating with him many times, speaking kindly, but in the end, it was impossible. If there had been even the slightest chance of dialogue leading to an alliance, we might have considered it, but the reality was that it never worked. In the first world, he even declared world domination and rampaged. To make matters worse, he underestimated the Waves. What happened after that… I remember we won, but my memory is a bit hazy. When we went to Siltvelt, he apparently tried to attack us as retaliation for the death of the fox that had disguised itself as one of his Seven Star Heroes.

To begin with, what right does he have to complain when he was hiding the fact that he killed a Seven Star Hero? Then, when the Four Guardian Beasts revived and the world was in crisis, instead of cooperating to fight them, he ambushed us in the chaos. Had he chosen to negotiate, even a little, and helped defeat the Four Guardian Beasts, he might have extended his lifespan. But he never listened. Every time, he resorted to the same foolish tactic—firing indiscriminately. If his weapon was taken away, he’d scream to have it returned. If his true identity was exposed, he’d abandon reason and attack us outright. They were beyond saving.
“To answer your question, your brother is not nearly as strong, kind, great, or noble as you think. All we did was expose his crimes in front of someone more powerful than him.”
Father shrugged slightly, sounding exasperated.
“Buhii! Buhibububu!”

“It’s not a lie. Can’t you see the evidence? Your brother is the kind of person who would kill innocent people without hesitation if it benefitted him. And in the end, he became a murderer who slaughtered the very chosen Heroes meant to protect the world.”
“Bubu! Bububububu! Bububu!”
“You’re going to save your big brother and kill us? Impossible. Didn’t your brother say it himself? That battles are won with quality, quantity, and strategy? You agreed with him too, didn’t you?”
That is entirely true.

“In terms of quality, we Four Holy Heroes are stronger. In terms of quantity, you have no numbers since you turned the country against you. And in terms of strategy, we won simply by exposing your brother’s crimes, leading to your punishment. In fact, this isn’t even strategy—this is just the result of his own misdeeds. If you want to blame someone, blame your brother.”

Father spoke with an expression of sheer exasperation. It’s true that we fought against Takt and played a role in capturing him, but everything that happened after that was simply the consequence of his own actions.
“If you claim you were just an ignorant victim, the country might still help you. Just like those people over there.”

Father turned his gaze toward a group of pigs shouting and throwing trash at Takt’s projected image. Of course, that alone wouldn’t absolve them. The pigs had even started fighting amongst themselves. Even among them, there was infighting—it was disgusting.
